title: Praise for God's Works
overview: Psalm 111 is a hymn of praise celebrating the greatness, faithfulness, and righteousness of God as revealed through His mighty works and covenant faithfulness. The psalmist commits to wholehearted praise within the community of the upright, emphasizing the enduring nature of God's righteous acts and commandments. This chapter highlights God's gracious provision, power, and redemption, underscoring the eternal reliability of His covenant. Positioned within the Book of Psalms, Psalm 111 serves as a theological reflection on God's character and His relationship with His people, encouraging believers to fear the Lord as the foundation of wisdom and understanding. Its poetic structure and acrostic form invite meditation on the nature of divine truth and the call to worship.
structure:
**Verses 1-2: Declaration of Praise.** The psalmist opens with a personal commitment to praise God wholeheartedly among the upright, acknowledging the greatness of God's works sought by those who delight in them.

**Verses 3-5: Description of God's Works and Character.** These verses describe the honorable, glorious, and compassionate nature of God's works, highlighting His provision and covenant faithfulness toward those who fear Him.

**Verses 6-8: Demonstration of God's Power and Faithfulness.** The psalmist recounts God's display of power to His people, the truth and justice of His works, and the eternal stability of His commandments.

**Verses 9-10: Redemption and the Fear of the Lord.** The final verses emphasize God's redemptive action, the holiness of His name, and conclude with the foundational truth that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, linking obedience to understanding and eternal praise.

keyVerses.text: Praise ye the LORD. I will praise the LORD with my whole heart, in the assembly of the upright, and in the congregation.
keyVerses.significance: This verse sets the tone for the entire psalm, expressing wholehearted praise within the community of the faithful, emphasizing worship as both personal and corporate.

keyVerses.text: He hath made his wonderful works to be remembered: the LORD is gracious and full of compassion.
keyVerses.significance: It highlights God's grace and compassion as central to His character, reminding believers that His mighty works are not only powerful but also merciful.

keyVerses.text: The works of his hands are verity and judgment; all his commandments are sure.
keyVerses.significance: This verse affirms the truthfulness and justice inherent in God's actions and commandments, underscoring their reliability and divine authority.

keyVerses.text: He sent redemption unto his people: he hath commanded his covenant for ever: holy and reverend is his name.
keyVerses.significance: It proclaims God's redemptive work and the eternal nature of His covenant, linking redemption to the holiness and reverence due to His name.

keyVerses.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.
keyVerses.significance: This concluding verse connects reverence for God with true wisdom and understanding, encouraging obedience and promising enduring praise.

characters.name: The LORD
characters.description: The central figure of the psalm, God is portrayed as mighty, gracious, compassionate, righteous, and faithful to His covenant. His works and commandments are the basis for praise and wisdom.

characters.name: The Psalmist
characters.description: The speaker who commits to praising God wholeheartedly within the community of the upright, serving as a model of worship and reflection on God's attributes.

characters.name: The Upright/Believers
characters.description: The community of faithful individuals who seek and delight in God's works, serving as the assembly where praise is offered and wisdom is cultivated.

themes.description: The chapter emphasizes wholehearted praise of God in community, highlighting worship as a response to God's mighty and gracious works.
God’s enduring covenant and remembrance of His people’s needs are central, illustrating His steadfast love and commitment throughout generations.

themes.theme: Wisdom and the Fear of the LORD
themes.description: The psalm concludes by linking the fear of the Lord with the beginning of wisdom, connecting reverence for God with understanding and obedience.
The psalm celebrates God's powerful works as true and just, affirming the reliability and righteousness of His commandments.

historicalContext: Psalm 111 is part of the Hebrew Psalter, traditionally attributed to the post-exilic period though possibly drawing on earlier worship traditions. It reflects a time when Israel was focused on reaffirming God's covenant faithfulness and the importance of communal worship after periods of national crisis. The psalm’s emphasis on assembly and uprightness corresponds with the restored temple worship in Jerusalem, where public praise and instruction in the law were central. Geographically, it is set within ancient Israel, where the covenant relationship with Yahweh defined social and religious identity. Politically, this period was marked by Persian rule, allowing the Jewish community to rebuild and reestablish religious practices.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology sees Psalm 111 as a celebration of God's sovereign works and covenant faithfulness, emphasizing the doctrine of God's providence and the believer’s call to worship and obedience as evidence of true wisdom.

Dispensationalists interpret this psalm as highlighting God's consistent dealings with His covenant people, often viewing the heritage of the heathen as a future promise fulfilled in the millennial kingdom.
Early church interpreters viewed Psalm 111 typologically, seeing Christ as the fulfillment of God's covenant and wisdom, with the psalm’s praise pointing to the ultimate redemption through Jesus.

crossReferences.connection: Echoes the theme that the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, reinforcing the psalm’s concluding truth.
Connects to the certainty and effectiveness of God's commandments and word, as described in Psalm 111:7-8.
Relates to God’s covenant faithfulness and mercy to those who fear Him, as mentioned in Psalm 111:5.
Encourages believers to offer acceptable worship with reverence and awe, resonating with the psalmist’s call to praise in the assembly.
Affirms the irrevocability of God's gifts and calling, paralleling the psalm’s emphasis on the eternal nature of God’s covenant.

application: Commit to praising God with your whole heart in both private and corporate worship settings.
Meditate on God’s works as evidence of His righteousness and faithfulness to strengthen your trust in Him.
Cultivate a reverent fear of the Lord as the foundation for wisdom and godly understanding.
Obey God’s commandments as a demonstration of your faith and as a means to receive His blessing.
Remember God’s covenant promises to encourage perseverance in trials and assurance of His provision.
Praise God continually, recognizing His holiness and redemption in your daily life.
conclusion: Psalm 111 stands as a timeless hymn of praise that calls believers to recognize and celebrate the greatness, faithfulness, and righteousness of God. It intertwines worship with theological reflection on God’s covenant and works, encouraging a reverent fear that leads to wisdom and obedience. This psalm invites Christians today to join the assembly of the upright in wholehearted praise, trusting in the eternal reliability of God’s promises and commandments. Its enduring message strengthens faith, deepens understanding, and inspires continual worship of the holy and compassionate Lord.

definitions.definition: In the KJV, 'meat' refers to food or sustenance, symbolizing God's provision for those who fear Him.
Truth or reality; in this psalm, it denotes the absolute truthfulness of God's works.
A reverential awe and respect for God that leads to obedience and wisdom.
An inheritance or possession; here it refers to the land or blessings given by God to His people.
Worthy of reverence or respect; describing God's holy and awe-inspiring name.
